groups.name: Page Purpose
groups.description: The Settings page is the central configuration hub for the entire runner application.

assertions.description: Users can access all application configuration from a single organized settings hub with categorized sub-pages
Users can navigate between setting categories using a secondary sidebar

groups.name: AI Provider Configuration Goals
groups.description: Users need to configure which AI providers and models power their automation workflows.

assertions.description: Users can configure AI providers with API keys and select models for workflow execution
Users can select default AI models and override per workflow

groups.name: Claude Account Switching
groups.description: The AI tab's Claude Accounts section supports multi-account management with automatic failover on rate-limit. Users can see which account is active, which are rate-limited, and manually switch between accounts. When in Least Usage mode, the runner auto-selects the best account at startup and auto-rotates on rate-limit during workflows.

assertions.description: The Claude Accounts section is visible within the AI Providers tab, showing a Users icon and 'Claude Accounts' heading
assertions.precondition: AI Providers tab is selected

assertions.description: The currently active account (used by the runner at runtime) displays a blue 'Active' badge. Exactly one account should have this badge at any time when accounts are configured.
assertions.precondition: AI Providers tab is selected and at least one Claude account directory is configured

assertions.description: Non-active accounts show a 'Switch' button that allows manually switching to that account. Clicking Switch calls the switch_claude_account Tauri command, clears any cooldown on the target account, and refreshes the live account state to reflect the new active account.
assertions.precondition: AI Providers tab is selected and at least two Claude account directories are configured

assertions.description: When an account has been rate-limited (hit token/usage limits), it displays a red 'Rate-limited' badge. The badge appears based on live backend state from get_claude_accounts, not from the usage check.
assertions.precondition: AI Providers tab is selected, at least one account is in cooldown from a rate-limit hit

assertions.description: When two or more accounts are configured, a Selection Mode section appears with Manual and Least Usage options. Least Usage mode description reads 'Auto-select & failover on rate-limit', indicating the runner will auto-select the best account at startup and auto-rotate when one hits a rate limit during workflows.
assertions.precondition: AI Providers tab is selected and at least two Claude account directories are configured

assertions.description: When the Switch button is clicked, the targeted account's button shows 'Switching...' text with a spinning icon while the backend processes the switch. All other Switch buttons are disabled during this time to prevent concurrent switches.
assertions.precondition: User has just clicked Switch on a non-active account

groups.name: Agentic Behavior Goals
groups.description: Users fine-tune how the AI behaves during workflow execution.

assertions.description: Users can set maximum iteration limits to control AI execution

groups.name: Integration Configuration Goals
groups.description: Users configure external integrations like MCP servers, cloud relay, Playwright, and log sources.

assertions.description: Users can add MCP servers that provide additional tools to AI
Users can configure log file paths for error monitoring
Users can configure Playwright browser testing settings

groups.name: Data Management Goals
groups.description: Users manage storage, backups, and updates.

assertions.description: Users can create backups of their runner configuration and workflows
Users can check for application updates

groups.name: Claude CLI Authentication Status
groups.description: The Claude CLI section displays authentication status including subscription type and expiry countdown, with the ability to re-authenticate when needed.

assertions.description: The Claude CLI section displays current authentication status (authenticated or not) when the AI Providers tab is selected
assertions.precondition: AI Providers tab is selected

assertions.description: When authenticated, the subscription type (e.g. Pro, Team, Max) is displayed so users know their plan tier
assertions.precondition: AI Providers tab is selected and Claude CLI is authenticated

assertions.description: An expiry countdown is shown indicating when the current authentication session expires, helping users plan re-authentication
assertions.precondition: AI Providers tab is selected and Claude CLI is authenticated

assertions.description: A re-authenticate button is available that triggers a new authentication flow when clicked
assertions.precondition: AI Providers tab is selected

groups.name: Claude CLI Execution Configuration
groups.description: Users configure how the Claude CLI is executed: choosing an execution mode (auto, windows_native, wsl, native), optionally setting a custom executable path, and configuring a timeout for CLI operations.

assertions.description: An execution mode dropdown is present with options: auto, windows_native, wsl, native, allowing users to control how the Claude CLI binary is invoked
assertions.precondition: AI Providers tab is selected

assertions.description: A custom executable path input allows users to override the default Claude CLI binary location
assertions.precondition: AI Providers tab is selected

assertions.description: A timeout configuration field accepts values between 60 and 3600 seconds, controlling how long the runner waits for a CLI operation before timing out
assertions.precondition: AI Providers tab is selected

assertions.description: A launch command input is available per account, allowing users to customize the command used to invoke Claude CLI for each account directory
assertions.precondition: AI Providers tab is selected and at least one Claude account directory is configured

groups.name: Claude CLI Multi-Account Management
groups.description: The Claude CLI section provides multi-account management with live state badges (Active, Rate-limited, Auto-selected), color-coded usage bars (green <50%, yellow 50-80%, red >80%), switch buttons per account, and a Check Usage button to refresh usage data.

assertions.description: Each configured account displays a usage bar that is color-coded: green when usage is below 50%, yellow between 50-80%, and red above 80%, giving users a visual indication of remaining capacity
assertions.precondition: AI Providers tab is selected and at least one Claude account directory is configured and usage has been checked

assertions.description: Each account shows a live state badge reflecting its current status: Active (blue), Rate-limited (red), or Auto-selected, updated from backend state
assertions.precondition: AI Providers tab is selected and at least one Claude account directory is configured

assertions.description: A Check Usage button fetches current usage data from the Claude CLI for all configured accounts and updates the usage bars
assertions.precondition: AI Providers tab is selected and at least one Claude account directory is configured

assertions.description: The Claude CLI section root div has data-tutorial-id='ai-settings-panel' for tutorial targeting
assertions.precondition: AI Providers tab is selected

groups.name: Claude CLI Account Directory Actions
groups.description: Users can manage their Claude account directories: add new directories, remove existing ones, auto-detect available directories, and toggle between Manual and Least Usage account selection modes.

assertions.description: An add directory control allows users to register a new Claude account directory for multi-account management
assertions.precondition: AI Providers tab is selected

assertions.description: Each configured account directory has a remove button that deletes it from the multi-account configuration
assertions.precondition: AI Providers tab is selected and at least one Claude account directory is configured

assertions.description: An auto-detect button scans the system for existing Claude configuration directories and offers to add them
assertions.precondition: AI Providers tab is selected

assertions.description: When two or more accounts are configured, a selection mode toggle switches between Manual (user picks active account) and Least Usage (runner auto-selects the account with lowest usage and fails over on rate-limit)
assertions.precondition: AI Providers tab is selected and at least two Claude account directories are configured

groups.name: World State Verifier — Mode & Connection
groups.description: The WSV tab allows configuring the VLM-based World State Verifier (CUA-WSM / SEAgent 7B judge). The mode dropdown selects between Disabled (default), Enabled (WSM verdict wins), and Shadow (both run, text verifier decides, disagreements logged). Changes take effect on the next agentic verification iteration without a runner restart.

assertions.description: The page heading 'World State Verifier' is visible with a description mentioning VLM-based judge and CUA-WSM
assertions.precondition: World State Verifier tab is selected

assertions.description: A mode dropdown with data-content-label 'wsv mode' offers three options: Disabled, Enabled, and Shadow. Each option shows a one-sentence description below the dropdown when selected.
assertions.precondition: World State Verifier tab is selected

assertions.description: When mode is set to Shadow, a blue info banner appears recommending to 'run 10-20 agentic workflows' before flipping to Enabled. When mode is Disabled or Enabled, this banner does not appear.
assertions.precondition: World State Verifier tab is selected

assertions.description: An endpoint text input with data-content-label 'wsv endpoint' shows the llama-swap base URL, defaulting to http://127.0.0.1:8100
assertions.precondition: World State Verifier tab is selected

assertions.description: A model text input with data-content-label 'wsv model' shows the model alias, defaulting to 'cua-wsm'
assertions.precondition: World State Verifier tab is selected

assertions.description: Clicking the 'Test Connection' button (data-content-label 'test wsv connection') pings the configured endpoint at /v1/models with a 5-second timeout. On success, a green status shows latency and available model count. On failure, a red status shows the HTTP error. If the configured model isn't in the server's model list, a yellow warning appears.
assertions.precondition: World State Verifier tab is selected

assertions.description: Clicking 'Save WSV Settings' (data-content-label 'save wsv settings') persists mode, endpoint, model, and screenshot-evidence toggle via the save_wsv_settings Tauri command. The button text transiently changes to 'Saved!' with a green check icon for 3 seconds. A green banner 'Settings saved — changes take effect on the next verification iteration, no restart required' appears. Settings are also updated in-process via WsvConfig::set_global so the next agentic loop iteration picks them up without restart.
assertions.precondition: World State Verifier tab is selected

groups.name: World State Verifier — Screenshot Evidence Toggle
groups.description: A toggle controls whether downsampled pre/post screenshot thumbnails are embedded in the agentic verification iteration canvas panels when the WSM verdict is used.

assertions.description: A toggle switch for 'Screenshot Evidence in Iteration Panels' exists in the Evidence section, with a description about embedding downsampled pre/post thumbnails
assertions.precondition: World State Verifier tab is selected

assertions.description: A purple info banner explains thumbnails are capped at 320px wide (~20KB each) and that the toggle can be turned off to save DB space
assertions.precondition: World State Verifier tab is selected

groups.name: World State Verifier — Shadow-Mode Calibration View
groups.description: A calibration section shows recent disagreements between the WSM (VLM judge) and the text verifier agent from shadow-mode runs. Users review these to decide whether to flip from Shadow to Enabled mode. The section auto-polls every 10 seconds and supports filtering by status-pair pattern.

assertions.description: The calibration section has heading 'Shadow-Mode Calibration' with a BarChart3 icon and a refresh button (data-content-label 'refresh wsv calibration')
assertions.precondition: World State Verifier tab is selected

assertions.description: When mode is NOT Shadow, a yellow warning banner says 'Enable Shadow mode above and run a workflow to start collecting disagreement data'. When mode IS Shadow, this banner disappears.
assertions.precondition: World State Verifier tab is selected

assertions.description: Four filter chips exist: 'Any mismatch' (data-content-label 'filter-any'), 'Text pass / WSM refused' (data-content-label 'filter-text_pass_wsm_refused'), 'Text pass / WSM fail' (data-content-label 'filter-text_pass_wsm_fail'), and 'Text fail / WSM pass' (data-content-label 'filter-text_fail_wsm_pass'). Each shows a count badge. Clicking a chip filters the table below to show only matching disagreements.
assertions.precondition: World State Verifier tab is selected

assertions.description: When no shadow-mode disagreements exist, the table area shows 'No shadow-mode disagreements recorded yet.' with a data-content-label 'wsv calibration empty'. When mode is Shadow, an additional hint 'Run an agentic workflow to populate this view.' appears.
assertions.precondition: World State Verifier tab is selected and no disagreements exist

assertions.description: When disagreement rows exist, a table (data-content-label 'wsv disagreements') renders columns: Time (relative, e.g. '2m ago'), Task Run (ID truncated to 10 chars), Iter (iteration number), Text (status badge with confidence %), WSM (status badge with confidence %), Intent (truncated to 80 chars), and WSM Observations (truncated to 120 chars). Status badges use color coding: green for pass, yellow for partial, red for fail/unreachable, purple for refused.
assertions.precondition: World State Verifier tab is selected and at least one disagreement row exists

assertions.description: The calibration section auto-refreshes every 10 seconds. A footer line shows 'N row(s) loaded · auto-refresh every 10s'. The refresh button (data-content-label 'refresh wsv calibration') triggers an immediate reload.
assertions.precondition: World State Verifier tab is selected

groups.name: World State Verifier — Reset & Validation
groups.description: Edge cases and the Reset to Defaults flow.

assertions.description: Clicking 'Reset to Defaults' (data-content-label 'reset wsv defaults') sets mode to Disabled, endpoint to http://127.0.0.1:8100, model to cua-wsm, and screenshot evidence toggle to on. Changes are local until Save is clicked.
assertions.precondition: World State Verifier tab is selected

assertions.description: If the endpoint field is cleared (empty string), the Save button is disabled or clicking it shows an error 'Endpoint cannot be empty'. The page does not crash.
assertions.precondition: World State Verifier tab is selected and endpoint field is empty

assertions.description: If the model field is cleared (empty string), the Save button is disabled or clicking it shows an error 'Model cannot be empty'. The page does not crash.
assertions.precondition: World State Verifier tab is selected and model field is empty
